about: Ordinary matplotlib charts with sentences that are hard to read: negations, decreases, 'lower than' / 'trails', 'improves by 8.2%' (points or relative?), hedges on large numbers ('about 1000'), ranges '84-86%' and 'between', '±', number words, 'after 5 epochs', "X's accuracy".

claims.sentence: We trained each network for 10 epochs and repeated every run 3 times.
ResNet-50 does not exceed 92% accuracy at epoch 10.
ViT-S never reaches 90% accuracy at epoch 10.
At epoch 10, ViT-S trails ResNet-50 by 4.0 points.
At epoch 10, ViT-S trails ResNet-50 by 9.0 points.
From epoch 5 to epoch 10, the accuracy of ResNet-50 improves by 8.2%.
claims.why: ambiguous %: 8.2 points (true) but 9.9% relative; never a flag

claims.sentence: From epoch 5 to epoch 10, the accuracy of ResNet-50 improves by a relative 9.9%.
ResNet-50 reaches 83.0% accuracy after 5 epochs.
VGG-16's accuracy is 70.0% at epoch 3.
At epoch 10, VGG-16 reaches 84-86% accuracy.
At epoch 10, ResNet-50 reaches between 90% and 92% accuracy.
ResNet-50 reaches 91.2 ± 0.4% accuracy at epoch 10.
ViT-S reaches eighty-seven point two percent accuracy at epoch ten.
From epoch 1 to epoch 10, the loss of VGG-16 drops by 65%.
From epoch 1 to epoch 10, the loss of ResNet-50 drops by 30%.
From epoch 1 to epoch 10, the loss of ResNet-50 improves by 70%.
claims.why: 'improves' on a loss means it falls by 70%

claims.sentence: The loss of VGG-16 is 0.77 at epoch 10.
On GPU, ResNet-50 reaches about 1000 images per second.
claims.why: hedged large number: 1040 is within 5% of 'about 1000' (the old rule allowed only ±5)

claims.sentence: On CPU, VGG-16 reaches ~35 images per second.
On GPU, ViT-S reaches >700 images per second.
On GPU, VGG-16 reaches about 600 images per second.
